text:
Maria: quick proposal — move per-tenant routing & policy decisioning out of runtime into a tiny co-located sidecar agent. goal: decouple policy iteration from runtime deploys and reduce blast radius.

Ajay: interesting. main concerns: extra RPC hop, ops surface area, and consistency during outages. do we have a perf budget for an added hop? :thinking_face:

Jordan: if sidecar is co-located and uses loopback, extra latency should be negligible. still need to validate p99 and cold-start behavior. propose a small spike: 5k QPS across 50 tenants, measure p50/p95/p99, and tail effects under GC/CPU pressure.

Sasha: ownership question — infra builds and owns the agent, runtime integrates a minimal client shim. infra can iterate on policy logic without runtime releases. this also helps for private deployments where ops want control.

Maria: agree on ownership. design constraints: sidecar must expose /health, metrics, tracing, and a gRPC stream API for policy updates; runtime keeps a short-lived cache for fallback. policy must be versioned.

ci-bot: new CI job created: sidecar-canary-smoke (daily).

Ajay: rollout idea:
1) implement sidecar + compatibility shim in runtime (env toggle)
2) default still reads local policy; enable sidecar on a per-node feature flag
3) canary 5% nodes for 72h, monitor latency, error budget, policy-mismatch alerts
4) gradually increase and flip tenants; once stable, remove internal policy code

Jordan: failure modes to document: sidecar unresponsive, policy-stream lag, config desync across replicas. runtime fallback plan: consult local cached policy and route to fallback model variant; emit tracing span with fallback reason.

Sasha: starting proto sketch (keep tiny):
```
message Route { string path = 1; string model_variant = 2; }
message Policy { string tenant_id = 1; repeated Route routes = 2; int64 version = 3; }
service PolicyService { rpc Subscribe(SubscribeReq) returns (stream PolicyUpdate); rpc Get(PolicyKey) returns (Policy); }
```
We should keep the protocol backward compatible and allow a JSON-encoded opaque extension field.

Maria: perf target suggestion: p99 request latency increase <= 2ms and no more than 1% increase in error rate. also set policy cache hit target >= 99.9%. include tracing, policy-hit metric, and stream-lag gauge.

Ajay: include an observability checklist in RFC: spans (runtime->sidecar), sidecar metrics (connections, stream lag, update rate), policy cache hit/miss, rollback counter. add alert thresholds and dashboards.

Sasha: migration playbook needs quick revert steps: 1) toggle node-level env to force local policy, 2) remove tenant routing from sidecar for affected tenant, 3) ops run script to re-sync local policy. define alerts to watch: policy-mismatch, stream-lag > 10s, sidecar-restarts > 5/min.

Jordan: I'll schedule a 30-min design sync once the RFC draft is up. also allocate a 2-day perf spike for the infra/perf team to produce numbers and a short harness.

Maria: I'll write an RFC draft covering motivation, API proto, perf targets, failure modes, rollout and rollback, ownership, testing matrix, and required dashboards. pinging @Ajay @Jordan @Sasha for review. aim to share in 48h. :rocket:

Ajay: thanks — please include load generator config and tenant distribution assumptions in the perf section (burstiness, hot-tenant ratio).

Sasha: add a small acceptance test: simulate policy update storms and ensure no more than 0.1% of in-flight requests fail with stale policy.

Maria: noted. drafting now.
